rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> field experiment at Werer Agricultural Research Center in 2019/20, RCBD split-plot with drip vs furrow as main plots and four irrigation levels (100, 85, 70, 55% ETc) as subplots, three blocks, 27 plots. Q2: Results, Table 3 and text <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc yielded 16666.6 kg/ha vs 7078.2 kg/ha for conventional furrow at 100% ETc; authors state drip at 100% ETc increased maize grain yield by 57.53% compared to conventional furrow (farmers' practice).
rows.notes: Single site, single season, single crop; one method (plot harvest). No soil-water or other mechanism variable measured through the season (soil properties only characterised for scheduling); yield components reported but not a causal pathway variable. Economic section says drip at 100% ETc suits investors and AFI 70% suits small-scale farmers, but this concerns affordability, not a stated requirement for the yield effect. No limitations stated. Tables give LSD, CV and letter groupings only, no SD/SE/CI per treatment; CV of pooled experimental error judged insufficient as a dispersion measure for the claimed result (doubt noted).

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own field experiment at Werer, 2019/20, split-plot RCBD comparing drip and furrow irrigation at four ETc levels. Q2: Abstract and Results <U+2013> seasonal water applied was highest (701.7 mm) under conventional furrow at 100% ETc; authors state that drip at 100% ETc saved 33.7% of irrigation water compared to conventional furrow irrigation (farmers' practice), with WUE 2.15 kg/m3 for drip 100% ETc vs 0.60 kg/m3 for CFI (Table 3).
rows.notes: Water saving is derived from the scheduled/applied irrigation depths (computed from ETc, wetted fraction, application efficiency), not independently measured by a second method; no soil water balance, drainage or evaporation measured as mechanism. Single site/season/crop, plot scale. No limitations stated; only LSD/CV/letters reported for WUE, no SD or CI for the applied-water figures.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own split-plot field experiment at Werer, 2019/20, with alternate furrow irrigation (AFI) and drip (DI) at 100, 85, 70, 55% ETc plus conventional furrow control. Q2: Results text and Table 3 <U+2013> drip at 100% ETc (16666.6 kg/ha) vs alternate furrow at 100% ETc (4753.1 kg/ha); authors state a 71.5% maize yield increase for drip over alternate furrow irrigation at 100% ETc, with 24.58% more irrigation water applied under drip than AFI.
rows.notes: Claim correctly attributed to drip vs AFI comparison. Note that the study reports drip applied 24.58% more water than AFI (AFI applied less water by design), so the comparison is not water-neutral. One method, one site, one season, plot scale; no mechanism variable measured; no stated requirements or limitations; dispersion limited to LSD, CV and letter groupings.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary single-season field trial (2019/20) at one site in semi-arid Middle Awash, Ethiopia, comparing drip and furrow (conventional and alternate) at four irrigation levels on maize; results are plot yields, yield components, WUE and partial budget analysis. Some inconsistency in text: WUE maximum attributed to drip 100% ETc in abstract but to drip 85% ETc in results/Table 3.
